thread:
sam: Heads-up: nightly CI shows a P99 tail spike for tiny-batch small-sequence after we rolled PyTorch 2.7 + CUDA 13.1 images last night. A100 runs, seq_len=16, batch=1-4 worst.
lee: I can repro locally with the short bench. latency for some requests ~2x.
sam: repro command I used:
```
python bench_infer.py --model=gpt-small --seq_len=16 --batch-sizes=1 2 4 --device=cuda --runs=200
```
sam: nvprof + flamegraph point to an unstable matmul kernel choice and a KV prefetch kernel that keeps spiking. autotune seems to flip preferred matmul path every few steps.
niv: paste the profiler top lines? any trace link?
sam: top kernels (avg ms):
matmul_path_X (38%) 0.92ms
matmul_path_Y (33%) 0.81ms
kv_prefetch (26%) 0.68ms

sam: before the image bump we were stable on matmul_path_X. after the bump selection alternates and prefetch thrash correlates with tail latency.
marie: could be interaction between Triton autotune refactor we merged and CUDA 13.1 scheduler heuristics. I filed a Triton thread earlier.
lee: I ran a bisect across merges on our runtime: isolates to the Triton autotune selector refactor (PR 0x9a3f7) + a tiny runtime shim change that adjusted kernel scoring weights. Combined they produce the flip.
niv: try setting TRITON_AUTOTUNE_DISABLE=1 locally to confirm.
sam: confirmed: with autotune disabled kernel stays on X and tail latency returns to baseline. prefetch spikes gone.
ci-bot: nightly-perf 2026-03-17T03:10: FAILED perf gate: tinybatch tail latency +112% vs baseline.
marie: placing rollout hold on the new py2.7/cuda13.1 image. @ops please start canary rollback for affected clusters.
ops: acknowledge, starting rollback on canary clusters now. will monitor.
lee: quick mitigation that helped in my environment: pin the kernel via a runtime whitelist. snippet:
```
# temporary whitelist to stabilize matmul choice
triton.set_preferred_kernels({"matmul_layer": "matmul_path_X"})
```
will open PR with this as a short-term patch.
niv: longer term we should make autotune selection deterministic: deterministic tie-breaker and penalize churn. also add a churn detector so prefetch backs off if kernel choice toggles frequently.
sam: +1. KV allocator's prefetch heuristic should reduce prefetch aggressiveness when kernel churn > threshold so we don't thrash L2 and eviction patterns.
marie: plan: 1) ops rollback on canary (in progress), 2) lee pushes whitelist PR and CI perf smoke before promoting, 3) niv + sam open PR for autotune determinism and prefetch-churn backoff.
lee: I'll add a CI tiny-seq test (seq=16 batch=1) to guard against regressions in future. PR when ready.
niv: drafting autotune PR with tests that assert kernel stability under driver + triton combos. test plan includes 10k small requests and a churn monitor metric.
sam: uploaded a repro trace: //perf/trace/2414689012/tinyseq-autotune-flip.html
marie: once whitelist PR lands we'll validate canary metrics and then decide on promote vs keep rollback. please add notes to release changelog about the rollback reason.
ops: canary rollback completed. monitoring dashboards show tinybatch tail back within baseline +/-3%.
ci-bot: perf gate cleared on canary after rollback.
sam: postmortem to follow. hypothesis: Triton autotune refactor + CUDA13.1 scheduler tweak exposed non-deterministic kernel scoring; KV prefetch magnified it into a P99 spike.
marie: schedule short postmortem doc with timeline and mitigation steps. also block merging further autotune changes until we have deterministic tests.
lee: reminder for reviewers: prefer conservative autotune changes and include a deterministic fallback. :thumbsup:
marie: thanks for fast triage everyone. good job.
summary: Nightly CI showed a tiny-batch tail latency regression after PyTorch 2.7/CUDA 13.1 image roll. Root cause narrowed to Triton autotune selector refactor interacting with driver scheduling changes, causing kernel-selection oscillation and KV prefetch thrash. Canary rollback restored baseline. Short-term mitigation: whitelist preferred matmul kernel; long-term: deterministic autotune tie-breaker + churn-aware prefetch backoff.
